title: Process Events Using a Queue
real_world_story: A monitoring system receives events from multiple sources. Events must be processed in the same order in which they arrive so that no earlier event is handled after a later one.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Events arriving at the monitoring system
real_world_connection.target_represents: The event that should be processed next
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Using First-In-First-Out queue operations to process events in arrival order

problem_statement: Given a sequence of queue operations, process them using FIFO behavior. An enqueue operation adds an event to the rear of the queue, while a dequeue operation removes and returns the event at the front. Print the result of every dequeue operation.
task: Process all enqueue and dequeue operations and print the event removed by each dequeue operation.
input_format: The first line contains an integer Q, the number of queue operations. Each of the next Q lines contains either 'ENQUEUE X' to add event X to the queue or 'DEQUEUE' to remove the front event.
output_format: For every DEQUEUE operation, print the removed event on a separate line. If a DEQUEUE operation is performed when the queue is empty, print -1.

examples.input:
6
ENQUEUE 10
ENQUEUE 20
DEQUEUE
ENQUEUE 30
DEQUEUE
DEQUEUE
examples.explanation: Events are processed in the same order in which they were inserted into the queue.
The second DEQUEUE occurs when the queue is empty, so -1 is printed.

expected_algorithm.name: Queue Operations
expected_algorithm.reason: A queue follows FIFO ordering, making it suitable for processing real-time events in the exact order in which they arrive.

hint: Maintain a queue that stores incoming events.
Add an event to the rear during ENQUEUE.
Remove the front event during DEQUEUE.
real_world_takeaway: Queue operations are fundamental in event-processing systems where incoming events must be handled in their arrival order.
